statements.text: An example of our approach is the October 2022 advanced computing and semiconductor manufacturing equipment rule, which restricted the PRC's access to critical artificial intelligence integrated circuits, supercomputing capability, and semiconductor manufacturing technology. statements.text: the allure of AI is that it has the capacity to learn without human intervention, and human intervention can be slow and expensive and even emotional. [...] So my question is, how can financial regulators effectively oversee and evaluate something that is as fast changing as AI?

statements.text: So my question is these AI models are complex. They are opaque. This is the black box problem that you were alluding to in your testimony. statements.text: One of the things that I have been thinking about a lot is how do you overcome sort of the black box phenomenon of these AI models and how you get accountability around bias, for example.

statements.text: Dr. Inglesby, I would like to start with you. statements.text: Many of us are giving thought to how AI, artificial intelligence, is being deployed, and how we should be setting guardrails for its use [...] I think it is true that generative AI has gotten a lot of attention over this last year, both for its capacity and also for the limitations that have been on full view.

SCOOP: Major U.S. banks are detecting unauthorized third-party AI agents inside customer accounts, including some attempting to take actions that appear to be independent of user instructions, sources told Axios.

The findings have alarmed banking executives, who are racing to restrict access to their systems as AI moves at a velocity faster than financial institutions can respond, multiple industry and bank executives told Axios.

Several banks are now preparing for worst-case and even “day after” scenarios, including how to rapidly secure or restore customer accounts if things go wrong, the people said.

Several bank executives told Axios they're struggling to distinguish between human users and AI agents. One executive said banks also struggle to determine whether agents are authorized by customers or potentially operating without their permission, more akin to rogue agent behavior.
